answer: Assign every identity claim to a grading jury drawn from kin groups with no shared history with the author, so an attacker can never grade its own fakes. Like cargo at a wharf, each claim is inspected by strangers rather than the crew that brought it in. The jury checks the work's pulse — whether the identity actually did useful, verifiable tasks — and a lotus of trust only blooms when unrelated graders agree. To cheat, an attacker must capture many independent juries, each needing established reputation and staked funds, turning a cheap flood of fakes into a costly, slow campaign.
